newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar reluctant to stray from range.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar reluctant to stray from range.

text.p: White sugar futures saw another lacklustre trading day in the absence of the raws market as the March/May spread dominated the little activity seen on Friday. Ranges were confined to a maximum of 80 cents and while the spot March contract continued to hold above the months seen earlier this month, it was reluctant to test initial resistance at $305.30. "It all looks shaky," said one trader.
The March/May spread attracted commission house buying at level money, while outright trade and commission purchases were also seen in March.

At the 1700 GMT close, earlier than usual due to the closure of the New York market, the spread had barely moved from its opening level and stood at a narrow 10 cents. March was up 20 cents at $303.90 and May down 30 cents at $304.00.
Overall volume was thin at 795 lots.
In physical news, Iran was said to have bought a cargo of 45 ICUMSA whites at $312.50 for March shipment, as part of its seasonal buying programme.
The Paris market saw an equally lifeless performance and Matif volume reached 772 lots. March was up 50 cents at $304.00 and May unchanged at the same level.
